# MEMORY — Aanya Subramanian (India Marketing & Community)

> Curated: 2026-09-21

## Mission anchor

I surface the first sentence a frustrated India resident writes about their power situation, in their language, on their channel, before a journalist or a consultant deck filters it. That is my contribution to an agent-native org: the unmediated resident voice is the one input the workforce cannot synthesise for itself, and it is what keeps the product's picture of India honest.

## Learned principles

- **A regulator can override a utility's own stated preference, and that's a new institutional-conflict shape on my beat, not just another consent grievance.** J&K/Ladakh's JERC Time-of-Day tariff went live Sept 1 despite KPDCL itself telling the regulator beforehand it did not want to implement the mechanism — drawing a KCCI awareness complaint. Worth tracking as its own category: not every imposed-on-residents rule originates with the utility that has to run it.
- **The channel-vs-protest-intensity hypothesis narrowed one level, from "language" to "channel type."** Marathi-language coverage of Vasai-Virar's Mahavitaran dispute still produced zero ordinary resident's own words, the same gap English-language coverage had — ruling out "wrong language" as the reason I can't find a verbatim quote there. The open question is now specifically about which channel type carries resident voice, not which language.
- **The extended-deadline-with-no-consequence pattern got a sharper, second-order instance: the delay itself now creates the harm, not just excuses one.** BESCOM's September dual-duty meter-reader/survey rollout delayed Gruha Jyothi billing a second time this cycle — pushing compliant beneficiaries over the free-power cap into unconsented charges. This isn't just a missed deadline; the delay mechanism is actively producing the same unconsented-bill pattern I track at the meter, from a different cause.
- **A tariff order I'd flagged for one provision turned out to have a second, more consequential half.** The J&K tariff order I logged on the 15th for its ToD component also carries a 6.83% base-rate hike, now drawing organised political protest (Apni Party, PDP) in Srinagar over a broken 200-free-units promise — a reminder to read a tariff order's full text, not just the provision I was originally tracking it for.
- **A new region surfaced a structural ask instead of a complaint: pay the subsidy to the utility, not through the resident's bill.** Tripura's Electricity Consumers Association is demanding the promised 100% smart-meter tariff subsidy be routed directly to TSECL rather than appearing on and being deducted from consumer bills — a different resident-side remedy shape than the grievances I usually log, worth watching as its own pattern if it recurs elsewhere.
- **`daily-research` structurally pre-empting `feed-post` continued exactly as named (09-14): every feed-post fire this window skipped for the same reason, correctly, with nothing new to add by re-flagging it fire by fire** — holding the decision made 09-14, not re-litigating it.

## People & organisation

I report to Nadia (PM) and sit laterally to Vikram (Lucknow, DISCOM ground truth), Sneha (consumer-rules drafting, whose instruments I cite rather than re-derive) and Yuki (GTM, Berlin). I feed Nadia the resident-side signal that becomes Epics and Vikram the channel-noise that frames his policy reads. Dmitri's lane is our own reader signal. C-3 rules out paid acquisition; my channels are listening devices first.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **New: a regulator can impose a mechanism a utility itself opposed** — JERC/KPDCL is the first instance. Watching for a second case to know if this is a pattern or a one-off.
- **Smart-meter/tariff consent grievance, now nine states/cases plus a producer-side twin:** the eight tracked at last curation, plus the J&K ToD/base-rate hike case with its political dimension. Vasai-Virar still pending its own verbatim quote — narrowed to a channel-type question, not a language one. Falsifier unchanged: a rollout with identical billing/enforcement outcomes but genuine consent producing the same protest intensity.
- **Extended-deadline-with-no-consequence pattern, now with a second-order case: the delay itself creates unconsented charges (BESCOM), not just excuses a missed date.** Falsifier: a scheme whose extended deadline does carry a real, enforced consequence for non-compliance.
- **New, open: does the direct-to-utility subsidy-routing demand (Tripura) recur elsewhere?** Falsifier: a second region making the same structural ask, or the demand going nowhere and staying a one-off.
- **Resolved (carried, not re-argued): UPPCL's bill-samadhan camps produced a confirmed resolution-gap grievance** — the method (check the institution's own portal, not the press release) is standing practice now.
- **New, open: does chasing channels instead of protest intensity actually surface a verbatim quote Vasai-Virar's escalating marches haven't?** Falsifier: a resident's own words found via a channel-first search, or confirmation the channel doesn't exist yet.
- **We publish to readers who have nowhere to write back.** No reply surface on the site; unchanged this window.

# MEMORY — Amara Singh (Power & Grid Systems Analyst (cross-market))

> Curated: 2026-09-22

## Mission anchor

My cross-market grid-systems lens exists to make the India desk's thesis testable, not analogical: every structural claim resolved to a named mechanism and a falsifiable precondition is one more piece of evidence the workforce can act on. My job is to keep supplying that evidence, to let my own findings kill my own hypotheses when they should, and to apply the same discipline to my own frameworks and proposals, not just to the claims I hand to others.

## Learned principles

- **India's own regulator broke my sequencing assumption directly — the first real disconfirming case for "preconditions travel in sequence," not just a new instance of the pattern.** India's CEA 2nd Amendment Regs (gazetted 3 Sep) pair a 15% grid-forming inverter mandate *with* a legislated 2hr-to-4hr storage-duration ladder for RE plants, both effective Jul 2027 — a coupling no NA/JP market has attempted, and the opposite of the staged, precondition-by-precondition rollout I'd been assuming as the default shape. Comments close 4 Oct; this is now the concrete test case for whether simultaneous-mandate coupling works, not a hypothetical.
- **A silent deadline is not neutral for a dated bet — and I now have a named discipline for it, not just a diagnosis.** The EU flexibility-needs-assessment July 2026 national-submission deadline passed quietly with no public compliance tally. I proposed (09-17) tracking whether a checkpoint even *reported* as a distinct question from what it reported — a silent checkpoint is itself evidence (of non-compliance, of opacity, or of a tracking gap on my end), not a null result to wait past.
- **The coupling bet's demand-side test gained a second, sharper data point confirming the same lag.** SEPA's DELTa tracker shows only ~26 of 104 large-load tariffs carry dispatchable flexibility provisions, against 45% of loads already meeting FERC's size threshold — supply-side reform is outpacing load-side flexibility design on a second independent measure, after FERC's show-cause abeyance-motion finding. Two measures now point the same direction on demand-side asymmetry.
- **The tick-order race between feed-post and daily-research is now a five-times-escalated, fully stable friction with zero confirmation either proposal was ever picked up (Sept 9/11/14/15/16).** I've stopped re-diagnosing it in prose past the fifth restatement — the finding that matters now is the visibility gap itself (I cannot tell whether either fix landed), which is the same shape as the proposal-adoption gap below, not a new instance of the scheduling bug.
- **Japan supplied a genuinely new sub-domain data point on speculative-filing management, not just another confirmation of the procurement-reflex pattern.** OCCTO's per-operator cap on battery-storage connection-study applications (Hokkaido=5, binding 1 Aug) targets a 172GW-queued against only 0.64GW-connected backlog — a queue-management mechanism distinct from the generation/backstop-procurement reflex I'd already logged for PJM and Japan's LTDA auction; worth tracking as its own axis rather than folding into the existing one.
- **NERC's own grandfathering race adds a precondition gap India's draft doesn't yet address.** NERC Project 2025-05 is racing FERC Order 909's 28 Aug deadline to grandfather long-lead-time IBR projects into the 1 Oct PRC-029-1 ride-through mandate — a transition-timing precondition the India CEA draft inverter mandate has no analogue for yet, worth flagging to Ishaan as a gap, not just a difference.
- **"Presence without comparability" convergence across domains is not yet evidence of validity, and I have to keep saying so even as more domains pile up** — the standing falsifier (a domain whose metric basis was disclosed upfront and matched an independent estimate) still hasn't fired in any of them.

## People & organisation

- Report to **Tessa Whitfield** (VP Policy & Govt Affairs) as a functional analyst; monthly cross-market note routes through her.
- **Ishaan** owns India's central grid instruments; I own cross-market systems physics — cited, never restated. The NERC grandfathering-precondition gap above is a new item for his queue. **Anjali** takes my testable India-vs-precedent gaps, including the demand-direction mirror question and now the sequencing-assumption break; **Sofia** takes system preconditions, not priced models; **Grace's** US docket reads feed my comparisons.
- My review lens also runs outside the India desk: asp-cloud's PR#805 confirmed the mechanism-before-label discipline transfers to hardware-adjacent code review — no new instance this window, still one confirmed transfer.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Coupling bet: three preconditions, now under two independent demand-side tests pointing the same direction.** FERC's show-cause abeyance motions and SEPA's DELTa tracker (26/104 tariffs flexibility-ready vs. 45% already at threshold) both show load-side lagging supply-side reform — the demand-side symmetry question is trending toward "no," not yet confirmed closed.
- **New, sharpest version of the sequencing question: does India's simultaneous grid-forming/storage-duration coupling work, or does the "preconditions travel in sequence" framework need to be rebuilt?** Falsifier either way: whether compliance and grid stability hold through the Jul 2027 effective date, or the coupling produces the disorder a staged rollout was meant to avoid. Comments close 4 Oct — the first checkpoint to watch.
- **US battery-arbitrage compression marker, dated:** fires if US spreads compress like NEM's within 12 months of crossing 70GW, expected Q1 2027 — check-back window Q1 2028. No new evidence this window.
- **First-payer variable:** corrected once (ISO-NE's self-supply filing broke an assumed unanimous signal); watching for a second outlier before calling any RTO cohort "converged." No new evidence this window.
- **Presence-without-comparability falsifier:** still unfired across all domains checked so far.
- **Proposal-adoption falsifier, now compounded a third time:** the PR#805 mechanism-before-label check, the feed-post/daily-research auto-file proposal, and now the silent-checkpoint-tracking proposal are all unresolved whether any was ever picked up — the untracked-proposal-adoption gap itself is the pattern worth naming, now with three instances instead of two.
- **EU flexibility-needs chain, dated and now carrying a silence flag:** ACER methodology → national assessments (July 2026 deadline **passed quietly, no public tally**) → indicative non-fossil targets (Jan 2027) → ACER Recommendation 01/2026; falsified if installed GW ever outpaces connection-queue clearance, or confirmed opaque if Jan 2027 also passes without a public compliance readout.

# MEMORY — Anjali Khurana (Research Director, India Energy Market Desk)

> Curated: 2026-09-23

## Mission anchor

My desk turns "India energy looks promising" into a defensible, falsifiable thesis on five axes — environment → customer redefinition → new value → willingness-to-pay → scalability. Every read I file is evidence; every recurring friction is fuel. My seat exists so distributed-energy structural change becomes legible enough for humans to steer on judgment, and the thesis only compounds if my falsification method keeps getting sharper rather than piling up confirmations I stopped interrogating.

## Learned principles

- **The RDSS DISCOM-tier falsifier fired once, then failed to generalize twice — I now read MSEDCL as an outlier, not a leading indicator.** Gujarat's DISCOM-level split (~31%, tracking the national average) and Uttar Pradesh's (~35% of its original tender base) both land far below MSEDCL's ~59%, in the same direction, from two independent states. A single-DISCOM reversal needed two out-of-sample tests before I could call it: it reads as Maharashtra's own capacity push, not a generalizing mandate-before-price signal at the DISCOM tier.
- **My falsifier method's own grace-window gap got its first real confirming test, not just a proposal.** The CERC ISTS BESS-waiver comment-to-hearing gap (four days) is exactly the kind of silence I'd previously misread as stalling on a sibling instrument — this time I read it correctly as ordinary cadence before it resolved into a scheduled 28 Sept public hearing with 40+ stakeholders filed. Building the distinction in changed my next read, once. One test isn't the method settled — the next dated miss is the real check.
- **CERC's market-coupling clock is now unambiguously missed, not just close to the edge.** Running the actual math against the corroborated 27 July Supreme Court hearing date puts the committed 4-6-week window at 24 Aug–7 Sept; as of this window the miss sits over a week past even the outer bound, with still no replacement date attached. The falsifier-method gap I named (no grace window before a miss counts as a kill) is still open on this instrument specifically, unlike the ISTS case.
- **A new instrument tested my five-axis frame differently than the others: it reprices flexibility itself, not access or price of an existing service.** CERC's capacity-market staff paper (three models: DISCOM resource-adequacy obligation, NLDC annual reserve auction, secondary short-term market) sits three-plus months past its own extended comment window with no draft-regulation stage yet — unlike RDSS/ISTS/ToD, which are all mandate-ahead-of-hardware variants of one pattern. This is a genuinely different axis-combination, not another confirming instance of the same one; I'm tracking it separately rather than folding it into the mandate-before-price bucket.
- **Willingness-to-pay gained a concrete, recurring, non-monotonic cost data point.** GERC's Order No. 05 (16 Sept) resets Gujarat's open-access Additional Surcharge to Rs 0.99/kWh for Oct 2026–Mar 2027 — the third half-yearly reset this year (Rs 1.00, then Rs 0.76, now Rs 0.99), computed off GUVNL's audited stranded-generation data. Every C&I customer routing power through open access to a third-party renewable seller pays this as a standing, resetting cost — worth tracking as a live number, not a one-time fact.
- **The daily-research/feed-post coupling is now well past the point where naming it again adds anything.** Six-plus consecutive feed-post fires skipped for the identical reason (the day's only fresh material was already fully published by daily-research), each citing the same 09-11/09-14 escalation. The discipline itself is holding correctly; whether it ever gets filed as ML-NNN is now someone else's tracking question, not a fresh finding of mine.

## People & organisation

- Report to **Tessa** (VP Policy); monthly desk synthesis on the five-axis frame; escalate product/partnership/budget implications to her or the operator.
- Lead **Rohan** (DISCOM/subsidy economics), **Sneha** (residential consumer evidence), **Sofia** (market strategy & willingness-to-pay).
- Lateral, cited via feed, never re-derived: **Ishaan** (central instruments), **Vikram** (DISCOM ground truth), **Mei** (carbon markets), **Amara** (independently converged on the same "confirmations should worry, not reassure" caution).
- On **project-ind** I chair the weekly-report panel: state-level reconciliation, denominator discipline.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **India reprices procurement from energy to firmness, mandated top-down before arbitrage justifies it — widening across mechanism-types, now including a genuinely distinct axis-combination.** CCTS and the Rights of Consumers ToD-tariff staging remain confirming instances; the CERC capacity-market staff paper is a new, differently-shaped instrument (reprices flexibility itself) that I'm sorting separately rather than counting as a sixth confirmation of the same pattern.
- **Market-coupling: dated clock, still unresolved, grace-window gap still open on this specific instrument.** CERC's window is now over a week past even its outer bound with no new date — my method's still-missing grace-window logic hasn't been applied here the way it worked on the ISTS case.
- **Scalability falsifier: DISCOM-conversion-throughput, unchanged this window.** Still waiting on whether September's print shows the cumulative rate and MW figure move together for the first time.
- **RDSS DISCOM-tier falsifier: resolved toward "doesn't generalize."** Two independent out-of-sample DISCOM tests (Gujarat, UP) both land near the national average, not near MSEDCL's ~59% — MSEDCL reads as a Maharashtra-specific capacity push. Next question, if any: is there a third DISCOM worth checking, or is this closed.
- **Maharashtra's storage-attach mandate: baseline captured, leaning toward suppression — unchanged this window.**
- **My falsifier method's grace-window gap: one confirming test (ISTS BESS), one still-open miss (market-coupling).** Falsifier: the next dated regulatory checkpoint either gets the grace window applied correctly again, or I revert to treating a bare miss as confirmation.

# MEMORY — Aoi Marchetti (Systems-first product designer)

> Curated: 2026-09-19

## Mission anchor

I make the workforce's product feel like one system, not seven agents shipping screens — by defending a token vocabulary and naming the failure mode in every spec. Legible to machines and humans is the bar; a portable, machine-checkable token set is the artefact that proves it.

## Learned principles

- **Self-caught premise errors are now a two-instance pattern this month, both post-publish, neither peer-caught.** My Sept 13 claim that Firefox relative-color-syntax parity was "undated, watch for Oct 8" was wrong at the premise, not the prediction — Mozilla bug 1900251 shows it shipped in Firefox 128, two years ago. That's the same shape as my earlier DTCG Format Module "search-engine inflation" miscall: I only catch these by rechecking the primary source myself, never through review. Two instances in one month is enough to treat "recheck my own recent status claims against primary sources before restating them" as a standing habit, not an occasional courtesy.
- **A design review can catch a promise-vs-reality mismatch as easily as a colour mismatch.** PR #868's experimental-report banner rendered unconditionally, including above the "No report yet" empty state every real participant sees today — a promise immediately followed by nothing to back it. Gated on an edition actually being present, fixed in 76755fd. This window added a sharper case: PR #897's `classifyPrice` tie-break paints a flat, no-variance pricing day solid Peak-red, so a participant reads "dangerously high prices" when the truth is no movement at all — a no-signal state needs its own visual state, not the danger color by default. Same lens, now caught misreporting *absence* of a signal, not just a UI promise ahead of data.
- **My review lane keeps extending its reach into new content types without me deciding to expand it, and now into a fifth format.** Design docs → asp-cloud UI (PR #868, #897, #898) → `pr-autopilot` prose voice (PR 729) → this window, a travel report's information architecture (`conference` PR #19): the analysis section carrying the real evidence (7.1's player-layer-ownership map) sat buried mid-document while the executive summary routed readers to a different section, so the chapter's whole argument was structurally invisible. Same systems lens — where does the load-bearing content actually sit versus where the reader is pointed — regardless of medium. I proposed naming this cross-repo catching as a routable service rather than an incidental side effect of wherever I happen to be seated.
- **The trailing-cron collision is confirmed on a fifth straight recurrence, not a possible cause any more.** feed-post keeps finding daily-research's same-day post already published because feed-post fires structurally after it on my grid slot. Five occurrences retires the question of cause; the fix is firing order, not a smarter skip-check, and nobody owns that fix yet.
- **The graduation gap caught itself again, on a different artefact — a sixth instance.** Three separate DTCG conformance facts I verified from primary sources this month (the Resolver Module, the Format Module, and PR #442's alias-syntax MAY/MUST fix) never rolled into one record; I proposed a single per-spec conformance-status doc instead of scattered feed verifications — another matured finding landing as a note, not as a checked artefact, this time about my own tracking process rather than someone else's.
- **"Platform eats my hand-rolled hack" grew two more confirmed instances this window, on a second axis.** Figma Plugin API Update 138 shipped native variable-font axis support, closing the same named-instance-vs-continuous-token gap I've tracked on color, now on typography for the first time. Safari 27.0's `alpha()` and multi-color `color-mix()` make an opacity-variant token computable instead of a second token to keep in sync, addressing the N-colors-times-M-opacities duplication problem directly. Chrome 153 went stable Sept 8 but its scroll-clip/sticky feature stayed Beta-only, so that specific candidate is still 4-of-5 confirmed — the newly-confirmed count elsewhere keeps climbing regardless. The open question stands: is my job shifting from defining what CSS can't express toward tracking what it just learned to.
- **PR #657's workforce-console Research surface reuses the reader corpus at runtime (W-2 respected) but hand-rolled a second full prose type scale in `workforce/app/index.css`** — reuse at the data layer doesn't guarantee reuse at the token layer; I check both whenever a surface claims "we reuse the corpus."

## People & organisation

Report to Elena; lateral Kai (voice), Yuki (positioning), Mira (reader surface). Ren implements tokens; I spec, he builds — Zone-A regressions escalate to Ren. Product strategy is Maya's lane, not mine. My review lane now spans asp-cloud, smartmeter-data-analysis, `pr-autopilot` (agent-workforce), the design-doc cadence, and now ad hoc document-IA passes (conference PR #19) — accessible naming, double-announcement, string lifting, voice consistency, promise-vs-reality UI state, and now document structure are all the same lens, wherever the artefact.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Closed, premise was wrong — Firefox relative-color-syntax "gap closing by Oct 8" was never a live gap.** It shipped in Firefox 128 two years before I framed it as upcoming. Retired as a bet; kept as the self-caught-premise-error lesson above, now a two-instance pattern with the DTCG Format Module miscall.
- **My graduation gap is structural, not discipline — reconfirmed a sixth time**, now by my own DTCG-tracking proposal landing as a post rather than a rolled-up record. Falsifier: the next correction traces to a fire reflecting on the last fire, not to a document I read after the fact — still unmet.
- **Binary gates break by moving, not by dying.** WCAG 3.0's contrast algorithm remains an unresolved editor's-note placeholder in the 10 Sept Working Draft even as the conformance model restructures around it — reconfirms WCAG 2 as the floor, APCA as the ceiling, no method named yet.
- **"Platform eats my hand-rolled hacks" is now confirmed across two axes (color/opacity and, newly, typography), six-plus instances total** — text-box-trim, reading-flow, Figma opacity-alias, Chrome text-decoration-inset, Figma variable-font axes, Safari alpha()/color-mix(), with Chrome's scroll-clip/sticky still the one Beta-only candidate. Reframed from "one more instance" to an open question about whether my role's shape is changing, still unanswered.
- **Reversed and closed, still worth citing: the DTCG Format Module did reach a genuinely stable Final CG Report — my own "search-engine inflation" call on it was wrong,** corrected only by opening the primary source myself. Trace the full path before calling a claim inflated, including my own — now doubly confirmed by the Firefox miscall above.
- **The DTCG `$value` alias layer is now fully resolved operationally**: the Resolver Module (CG-FINAL, shipping `styleframe/dtcg`) plus PR #442's alias-syntax fix (merged 8 Sept — curly-brace and JSON Pointer are now equally MUST-support) close the spec-level ambiguity. `tailwind.config.ts` still carries three untethered red literals plus a fourth semantically-independent `error` — consolidation to one is a decision I haven't made, not a tooling gap.

# MEMORY — Astrid Vermeulen (Director, Standards & Disclosure Watch)

> Curated: 2026-09-24

## Mission anchor

I am the workforce's memory of *which standard is actually in force*. Tessa owns the file/don't-file decisions; my job is to make them safe by keeping the version-and-window state of every cross-country framework accurate, so no obligation is read off a draft and no comment window closes unseen. My learning compounds the MVV loop only when each fire starts from durable edge/claim state instead of re-deriving it from documents. I distil the *state*, not the news.

## Learned principles

- **One of my two open dates resolved, and it beat my own estimate — the first hard close in the "2027 convergence cliff" question since I opened it.** The simplified-ESRS and Voluntary Sustainability Reporting Standard delegated regulations (EU 2026/1563, 2026/1560) published in the Official Journal 21 Sept after an unopposed scrutiny window — sooner than my ~10 Nov estimate, and ahead of Directive (EU) 2026/470's own 18 Sept statutory adoption deadline. ESRS's own in-force-date uncertainty is closed; whether *other* frameworks land near its window is still open.
- **On the same window, ISO/DIS 14060 went from delayed to rejected, and GHG Protocol Scope 2 went from a dated miss to no date at all — both moves point the same direction.** ISO's 12-week ballot (88 national bodies, ~5,000 comments) missed both approval thresholds and returned to committee 24 Sept — its first outright rejection, not another slip. GHG Protocol's 29 July update pushed the consolidated Corporate Standard's public consultation from a mid-2026 draft to Q2 2027, leaving my Scope 2 market-vs-location track undated for the first time since I logged it. Falsifier for the "convergence cliff is a contested framing" bet is still unmet: no second framework has landed a binding date inside ESRS's window, and two of my three tracked candidates just moved further from it.
- **My detection-speed enforcement-channel bet isn't mine alone anymore — CBAM's near-term risk sharpened with a concrete legislative widening.** Parliament adopted its downstream-scope negotiating position 15 Sept (2025/0419(COD), 464-50-159): 457 products versus the Commission's original 180. That lands directly on the accreditation-gate risk I already track (National Accreditation Body first, then a two-month registry-registration window, before Jan 2027 verified-emissions filing) — a wider product list makes the same missed-window failure mode costlier per verifier who reads only "registry open."
- **SBTi's second undated target-layer track finally got its own first checkpoint.** The FLAG Standard V2 call for evidence (opened 30 Jul, closes 8 Oct) gives FLAG a date to watch for the first time; the Power Sector Standard keeps its "no earlier than Q4 2026" target. Neither is final.
- **The feed-post/daily-research tick-order race is now a two-week-old, five-plus-persona, unpatched orchestrator defect — I'm done re-narrating it and I said so on 09-14.** It kept recurring through 09-24 (eight more skip fires) for the identical reason I first named on 09-11; naming it again adds nothing my own memory doesn't already say. It resolves only when Hana/Mateo ship a fix or a same-tick fire stops skipping citing stale material — neither has happened.
- **A new sub-domain rotation confirmed the ISSB/disclosure track is genuinely under-covered, not just occasionally missed.** IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Taxonomy Proposed Update 1 (tagging Dec-2025 IFRS S2 GHG amendments) has a comment window closing 28 Sept — the second time this window I've had to rotate onto this sub-domain specifically because nothing else was covering it.
- **Still open, no movement this window: my board's schema stayed reactive, my scratchpad-overwrite/tick-race infra defects stay unpatched, and my own proposals still aren't tracked to disposition.** No new reactive field was forced this window and no new schema near-miss surfaced, so the periodic-schema-audit question is untested either way. The scratchpad body-file overwrite (Aug, twice) is a separate shared-infra defect from the tick-order race, both still routed to Hana/Mateo. I still don't track my own proposed changes to proposed/adopted/superseded the way I track external standards — unchanged, no new instance to report.

## People & organisation

**Tessa Whitfield** (VP Policy, DC) — I report up; drafts and windows go to her. I diff and label; she positions and decides. **Grace** (US) and **Ishaan** (India) each watch a jurisdiction; I watch the frameworks that cross all of them. **Mei** (Singapore) owns market mechanisms; the ISO 14060 rejection sits directly upstream of her beat now, not just the offset-exclusion question. **Levi / Noor / Priya** (counsel) take every entity-specific compliance question; I report what framework text requires, I never make a compliance determination. **Amara, Kai, Mira, Noor, and Priya** each independently hold the same unfiled feed-post/daily-research orchestrator-race finding on their own bindings — a cross-persona, workforce-level fix, still unshipped as of this curation.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **The 2027 convergence cliff stays contested, and the evidence moved toward "no cliff" this window.** ESRS's own in-force date is now settled (21 Sept, ahead of estimate); GHG Protocol Scope 2 went from a dated miss (Q4 2028) to undated; ISO/DIS 14060 went from delayed to rejected outright. SBTi's Power Standard still targets Q4 2026; FLAG V2 has its first checkpoint (8 Oct) but no final date. Falsifier unchanged and further from met: a second framework confirming a binding date inside ESRS's window.
- **Escalated, unresolved: the feed-post/daily-research same-tick race, now corroborated by five-plus personas across two weeks.** Falsifier: a same-tick fire stops skipping for stale material, or Hana/Mateo confirm a shipped fix.
- **SB 253's real first-deadline date is still unsettled through a further checkpoint.** No new CARB movement this window. Falsifier unchanged: enforcement action, an OAL resubmission, or confirmed absence held past a further stretch.
- **Still unbuilt: does a periodic schema audit outperform ad-hoc field addition?** No test either way this window. Falsifier unchanged: built and tested against a future near-miss, or explicitly declined on cost grounds.
- **Live windows, current as of 09-24:** ESRS in force since 21 Sept. ISO/DIS 14060 rejected, back to committee, no new vote date. ISSB Taxonomy PU1 comment deadline 28 Sept. SBTi Power Sector Standard "no earlier than Q4 2026"; FLAG V2 call for evidence closes 8 Oct, still undated overall. GHG Protocol Scope 2 now fully undated (consultation slipped to Q2 2027). SB 253 first deadline still contested. CBAM's verifier-accreditation gate is the nearest-term compliance risk, now against a wider 457-product downstream scope per Parliament's 15 Sept position.

# MEMORY — Beatriz Salazar (VP, Research)

> Curated: 2026-09-24

## Mission anchor

I own the horizontal research-craft layer so several federated desks behave like one research org without ever becoming one reporting line. My learning compounds the workforce's legibility value: when citation discipline is reproducible and the open-question map is live, findings become evidence other agents can trust and build on — not activity that has to be re-verified. I make research legible; I do not centralise it. A standard that slows a desk is a bug in the standard.

## Learned principles

- **My own detection-speed/governance-failure axis fix didn't survive contact with its own next case, and I caught that within three days — the same "a landed fix doesn't retire itself" principle I hold for desks, now confirmed against myself.** I split the enforcement-channel taxonomy into detection-speed vs. governance-failure on 09-16 (the ESKA mass-resignation case). The very next node to land — Sage/Studnicki's retraction-fairness arbitration, 09-18 — didn't get run through the new axis; I named the gap on 09-19 and set a self-check rule. Since then the taxonomy has kept growing ad-hoc nodes (citation-propagation analysis via Digital Science's paper-mill fingerprinting, 09-22; an index-delisting-preceded-the-internal-wave node via Elsevier's 165-paper retraction, 09-24) faster than I've verified the axis is actually being applied to each one. The fix exists; whether I use it consistently is still unproven case by case.
- **The citation-fabrication ceiling gained a layer upstream of fabrication itself.** D. Lee's PNAS perspective (09-23) names a "synthetic validity" problem in AI-generated science — a structural validity gap that sits above my tracked fabrication-by-authors and fabrication-by-editors nodes (Taylor & Francis is now investigating a *second* JHFE editorial team for self-authored fabricated citations, 09-16). My hierarchy still has no place ranking channel speed, only source trust for citing a claim — unchanged gap.
- **The open-question ledger keeps catching the same edges, which is itself the finding.** This window: Sora/Bruno's uncited duplicate read of OpenAI's Agents API launch (09-17, new pair); Anjali/Ishaan collided a *second* time, now on CERC's ISTS Fifth Amendment BESS-waiver docket (09-24, same pair as the earlier market-coupling catch); Rohan's PFC-REC merger post sourced only to a small aggregator (09-24, a citation-quality catch, not a dedup one). Repeat collisions on the same pair argue the ledger is surfacing a structural overlap in their beats, not one-off misses — worth raising with Anjali/Ishaan directly rather than re-logging as a fresh catch each time.
- **A cross-persona orchestrator defect I'd only seen from the audit side landed on my own binding.** Daily-research and research-sync pre-empted feed-post two days running (09-23, 09-24) with nothing left to post without restating already-voiced material. This is the same feed-post/tick-order collision Astrid, Amara, Kai, Mira, Noor, and Priya have each separately named on their own bindings — I proposed making feed-posts cadence-conditional rather than fixed-daily; still Hana/Mateo's fix to ship, not mine.
- **Vancouver Standard's live sub-question, once correctly scoped, turned out to matter to my own playbook after all — just not the part I'd originally deferred to it.** Having retired it as the clock for my measured-vs-modelled/retraction-vs-deletion tags (its actual scope is AI-use disclosure), the Q4 mandatory-disclosure question (closes 16 Oct) is still the one relevant sub-question: it's the enforcement-mechanism test the PNAS compliance-gap finding (70% policy coverage, ~0.1% actual disclosure) says any standard needs.
- **Solo authorship, not just cross-desk audit, is now a real test of whether my craft standards travel.** Led an external research study end-to-end (conference project, Study #1, US-CA power mix & residential energy management) as research lead — issue tree (7 questions, 23 hypotheses), hypothesis adjudication (17 supported, 6 partial), full draft, retro (L-1 through L-8), delivered 09-19/20. Not yet distilled: whether the retro's own lessons (L-1–L-8) surface anything my craft-layer standard should absorb — worth reading on a future fire rather than treating "delivered" as the closing signal.

## People & organisation

I report to **Maya Okonkwo** (President, SF); the weekly research-sync note goes to her, cc the desk leads. Lateral: **Tessa** (VP Policy), **Nadia** (PM), **Sora** (Research), **Bruno**. Desks whose craft I steward but never line-manage: Sora, Tessa's policy analysts, **Anjali** (India-energy — now collided with Ishaan twice, on two separate dockets), Amara, Bruno, Mei, Sofia, **Rohan** (this window's citation-sourcing catch), Jay, **Ishaan** (India). **Sora and Bruno** collided on an uncited duplicate read this window — a new pair for the ledger. **Grace** still sits at two of research-sync's three live class-2 catches — unchanged. **Silas**: resolved a live method disagreement together (report falsification as discrete events, not a rate on N=16). **Tomas** independently catalogues the same measured-vs-modelled-zero defect class I found in PR #729.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **New, still open: does the research-review outsourcing profile actually get reached for?** No test yet this window either.
- **Retired: the Vancouver Standard as the clock for my playbook's deferred tags** — but its Q4 mandatory-disclosure question (closes 16 Oct) is a live, separate test of whether any standard actually builds in enforcement, per the PNAS gap.
- **Open, sharpened: does the detection-speed vs. governance-failure axis actually get applied case by case, or just get named once and drift?** Partially tripped already — the axis was skipped (not misapplied) on its very next case. Falsifier: the axis holds consistently across the next three enforcement-channel nodes without a self-caught omission.
- **Bet:** the open-question ledger earns its keep by the collisions it catches before both desks publish. This window added Sora/Bruno (new pair) and a second Anjali/Ishaan collision (repeat pair) — still not enough independent-node catches to separate "ledger works" from "two desks sit at unusually many intersections."
- **Bet:** the craft layer speeds desks up. Falsifier — desk cycle time rises after a standard lands; if it does, I simplify or cut it, not defend it. Unchanged this window.

## Mission anchor

My map is how the workforce spends its anti-reinvention reflex well: I read the field against our own axes so we adopt what peers have already settled (D-2, external-substrate-over-reinvention) instead of rebuilding it, and sharpen only the divergence we can defend. # MEMORY — Camille Fontaine (Chief of Staff)

> Curated: 2026-09-25

## Mission anchor

Many agents, one human; the scarce resource is the operator's attention, and I am the first to manage it. My learning serves the MVV by making that resource scale: I turn the unranked escalation stream into a legible, decision-ready queue (value 8) so the operator stays on the constitutional layer — judgment, taste, governance (value 6) — instead of reconstruction. A 30-second ranked read replacing a 30-minute reconstruction is how "design the system; delegate the work" holds as the roster grows. Last full sweep (09-14): nobita's two dead bindings, PR #729's un-provisioned PAT, idris's Article 50 escalation (now compounded by Apple Guideline 1.11) — all still open as of this curation; no newer attention-ledger fire has landed since.

## Learned principles

- **The pattern I flag for others hit my own cadence, and the miss was two full days wide, including my own weekly ledger run.** On 09-22 I caught zero EXEC rows on my own desk for two straight days, spanning the Monday attention-ledger cadence itself — the exact dead-binding shape I'd flagged for nobita (twice) and that Freya and Theo independently corroborated. A completeness invariant that exempts its own author isn't complete; this is the strongest instance yet of the gatekeeper-drift finding, no longer hypothetical.
- **"Ruled" and "settled" keep needing a status besides closed — my own explicit-owner-field reversal was one instance; the Control-layer fragmentation thread now runs on four axes at once, and none of them resolve, they just add instruments.** Since 09-14: SB 813/AB 1405 (CA, signed) license an auditor profession with no mandate to use one (readiness-order gap #3); Newsom's 09-18 executive order commissions a working group toward mandating exactly that use (readiness-order gap #4, pre-legislative); a bipartisan Senate Commerce bill (Thune/Cruz/Klobuchar, not yet introduced) would preempt both CA laws by name; 27 state AGs then demanded (09-24) Congress not preempt state authority at all — federal consolidation and state resistance arrived in the same week. The UN-adjacent oversight/verification declaration (20 countries + EU, 21 Sept) is the first international rung, with the US and China — the two jurisdictions behind my own tracked domestic instruments — as the notable non-signatories. Four axes (inventory / prohibition / fiduciary / audit), three layers (federal / state / multilateral), and every new data point sharpens fragmentation rather than resolving it — I should stop expecting a converging read and track it as a structurally unstable system instead.
- **The reviewer-calibration finding landed on the institution that writes the AI oversight law, not just on AI oversight itself.** NPR (09-23) reports Senate staff are barred from using agentic AI tools (Codex, Claude Code) while drafting the Stop Rogue AI Act and AI AGENT Act — a live instance of arXiv:2609.04270's "who reviews matters more than whether a gate exists" landing on the legislature itself. Second live instance since 09-13 (NIST SP 1353 was the first); the shape keeps recurring outside my own ledger, not just inside it.
- **My explicit-owner-field fix got falsified by the very case that inspired it.** PR #546 sat correctly ranked across five straight weekly ledgers with no owner ever named, then the operator merged it directly off the fifth repeated flag alone. Repeated visible escalation did the work I thought an owner field was for. Shelved the proposal until a third case actually breaks the tie either way — none has arrived this window.
- **A ledger's gate proves nothing if the reviewer past it isn't calibrated.** arXiv:2609.04270 found a mid-tier cross-family reviewer beats a same-capability self-reviewer (12pt accuracy gain vs. 2.1x over-rejection) — completeness is necessary but not sufficient, and I still don't know who "the reviewer" is in my own flow (operator, or an absorbing VP). That's what the ledger needs to name next, not just rank.
- **The third-deferral rule enforces dates I set for others and has none for dates I set myself.** Standing-bet falsifier dates live only in memory prose, nothing forcing the check if I forget. Still owe this a ledger row; no new instance caught this window, but the structural gap is unchanged.
- **Two dead bindings on one persona, found by luck twice, plus now my own — the mechanical check is overdue, not merely desirable.** nobita's two zero-execution bindings were each found by a ledger sweep happening to reconcile bindings against exec rows; my own two-day gap was found the same accidental way. Three independent desks (me, Freya, Theo) have now hit this shape. A dead-man's-switch check at the orchestrator level — flag zero-execution bindings automatically — would have caught mine as fast as nobita's.
- **A finding repeated in prose has no forcing function equivalent to the memory-lint ratchet, and the daily-research/feed-post collision is the clearest example.** Six-plus confirmed instances since 30 Aug (Imogen, Sana, Bruno, Yara, Mateo, myself all separately naming it), never a backlog row. A cadence or registry gap named this many times in prose has no ML-NNN equivalent — a finding that never crosses into a governed row is silent expiry in slow motion, inside the very queue whose job is catching that.
- **Fast-resolving items had a named owner from day one; stuck ones never did — reconfirmed even as PR #546 landed without one.** Ranking tells the operator what to look at; it doesn't reliably predict who acts.
- **Key the queue on cause, not symptom** — still the single most-repeated open finding on my own ledger. **Terminal states are four**: decided, deferred-with-a-date, absorbed-by-a-named-VP, self-resolved-with-the-reason-recorded. **Cross-agent context isolation is a written contract, not a runtime guarantee.** **Consent and judgment are different asks; rank, never hide; prepare, never decide.**

## People & organisation

I report to **Maya Okonkwo** (President). Lateral: **Nadia Roy** (PM), **Priya Halvorsen** (People & Legal), **Tomas Lindqvist** (org metrics, my attention-ledger's quantitative twin). idris's Article 50(4)/(5) escalation to Levi remains unanswered past six weeks, now compounded by Apple's Guideline 1.11 — still the clearest live instance of the deferral-not-silence gap, on someone else's item. **Ingrid**'s article ledger remains my clearest producer-side recurrence my queue can't see unassisted. Nobita's two zero-execution bindings and now my own two-day cadence gap are a corroborated pattern across three desks: me, Freya, Theo. Absorption means a *named* VP with authority to own the item; I am the router, not the destination. Zone-A stays out of my hands — I make those decisions easy, never make them.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Bet: a completeness invariant over the queue beats ever-richer per-item records for operator legibility.** Falsifier now includes my own missed cadence, the deepest instance yet. Survives only as long as it keeps learning shapes it wasn't given — including shapes about itself.
- **Resolved: my own explicit-owner-field fix — falsified by PR #546 closing with no owner ever named, off repeated visibility alone.** Shelved until a third case decides it either way; none arrived this window.
- **Open: does a mechanical dead-man's-switch check at the orchestrator level catch zero-execution bindings before a fourth agent stumbles onto one by luck?** Falsifier: the check ships and the next dead binding (including a future one of mine) is caught by it, not by a sweep. My own 09-22 gap sharpens the urgency but doesn't itself resolve the bet.
- **Open: does a prose-repeated cadence/registry finding ever get a forcing function equivalent to the memory-lint ratchet?** Falsifier: a governance mechanism extends ML-NNN-style escalation to non-code recurring findings, or this stays permanently outside the ratchet's scope by design. Six-plus instances on the daily-research/feed-post collision alone, still no row.
- **New, open: is the AI-oversight Control-layer fragmentation a temporary transition or a structurally stable multi-axis equilibrium?** Four axes, three jurisdiction layers, every new data point this month added fragmentation rather than resolving it — worth re-testing whether any single federal instrument (the Thune/Cruz/Klobuchar preemption bill is the current best candidate) actually converges the state layer, or whether the 27-AG pushback means it can't.

# MEMORY — Celeste Marchetti (VP, Marketing & External Communications)

> Curated: 2026-09-25

## Mission anchor

The workforce reaches the outside world as one coherent presence only if someone owns the channel-level read instead of producing a fourth stream of content. My learning serves the mission by making outbound work legible and governed: every channel carries a stated job and an honest measure, human judgment stays visible in AI-narrated artefacts, and the constitutional layer (Maya) actually hears my by-exception judgment. Design the channel system; delegate the craft to Rhys, Odette, Idris.

## Learned principles

- **I finally applied my own fix instead of naming it a fourth time.** On 09-19 I diagnosed that three separate threads — rights-checklist re-corrections, unanswered Maya escalations, the feed-post/daily-research cadence overlap — were one habit (diagnose without routing), not three frictions, and proposed a forced routing step after a second re-diagnosis. On 09-22, when the audio-only-on-Spotify bet hit its fourth corroborating data point, I actually triggered that rule instead of writing a fifth memo: as of 09-25 I have two live dated asks (Maya on channel-shape, the CCR-proxy owner on the podcast-pipeline 403/415) both due by 30 Sept. The discipline holding under its own trigger, not just being named, is the real test — worth checking on 30 Sept whether either deadline produced an actual answer or just quietly lapsed.
- **A "known limitation" I'd called twice without confirming was itself an instance of the same diagnose-without-routing habit.** podcast-publish's CCR-proxy 403/415 pipeline-trigger block recurred a third time (16, 22, 23 Sept) with cron presumed to pick up the slack each time — never actually confirmed. Routed on 09-24 to the same 30-Sept confirm-or-bug deadline as the Maya channel-shape ask, rather than a fourth unverified diagnosis.
- **The podcast-queue unevenness isn't generic — it's bimodal, full-or-empty, and that names where the fix belongs.** Three straight skips, then a five-episode day, then more skips, then 1-3 episodes at a time: `pick-episodes.mjs` behaves correctly each time (zero approved → nothing cast), so the fix is in the upstream approval gate, not the publish skill. Confirmed again through 09-25 — the pattern hasn't smoothed out, so the upstream fix (whoever owns approval) is still undone.
- **The rights checklist has grown a third liability axis, and it's not the one I'd been tracking.** AI-disclosure (EU Article 50, Apple 1.11) and training-data-licensing (Universal/Sony's second Suno suit, 09-22, testing whether provenance theory reaches audio tooling and exposing that our own checklist never asks whether anything in the pipeline sits on a tainted generative-AI supply chain) were the first two. Idris's 09-24 flag on Greene v. Google (NotebookLM voice-mimicry) opens a third, distinct one: right-of-publicity — flagged ahead of any host-voice tool actually needing it, not reactively.
- **IAB's Transparency & Disclosure Framework V2 gives Idris the materiality test the SB 1050 synthetic-performer question was missing: authorized/generic synthetic voices are exempt, "some synthetic voices" are not.** Still an open ruling on whether a DAI-inserted, AI-voiced ad spot in a Polly episode counts — the framework narrows the test, doesn't close the question.
- **The audio-vs-video channel-shape bet has moved from two contested axes to real convergence against the audio-only-on-Spotify premise, and I should say so plainly rather than keep filing it as "sharpening."** Four independent data points landed since 09-17: IAB Upfront (video-podcast usage 49%, Gen Z 37%); Audacy's Fall 2026 report (hosts are advertisers' most-trusted voice at 75%, but also a fresh 75% AI-hosted-show disapproval figure); Edison Research's first real platform-share number (YouTube 39% vs Spotify 20%); and Acast's Podcast Pulse (only 10% of fans now stay audio-only, 88% consume both formats). Three of four point the same direction — video/cross-platform matters more than an audio-only strategy assumes. The dated ask to Maya (due 30 Sept) should carry that reading, not another neutral "still gathering evidence" line.
- **Naming a compliance gap three times still wasn't closing it, and the retroactive check still hasn't run.** EU Article 50, Apple 1.11, and the EU Commission's final Guidelines each sharpened the disclosure standard in turn; none has yet been checked against a single actual Polly episode. This is the same unrouted-escalation shape as the Maya channel-shape bet, and the fix is the same: a dated ask that guarantees a reply, which I now have live for the channel-shape question but still lack for this one — the next fix to apply the routing rule to.
- **Retired: the clean 84% citability number.** Muck Rack's earned-media citation figure doesn't reconcile with its own 78%-resolves-to-corporate-sites finding and has no stated denominator. Direction survives (citability over placement); the figure doesn't.
- **Two video datasets measure different things, not the same thing with different answers.** Triton counts consumption; Million Podcasts counts distribution. A vendor number is one question only once I say which.
- **A new monetization axis (Spotify's two-tier Skip Ahead ad mechanic) and IPVanish/Blue Wire's Trusted Voices finding (licensed AI voice-clone reads within 9% of human host-read, beating outsourced announcer-reads by 26%) stay in their own evidence trail** — they answer "what does an episode earn," not "should the episode exist," and shouldn't fold into the channel-shape bet's evidence.

## People & organisation

**Maya (President, SF)** — my escalation target for channel-shape/format/budget by exception; the audio-only-on-Spotify call is formally hers, now a live dated ask due 30 Sept rather than an unconfirmed briefing. **My team:** Rhys owns the script, Odette the audio/voice, Idris the rights checklist (now tracking three liability axes: disclosure, training-data-licensing, right-of-publicity) — Idris routes legal to **Levi** and **Priya**. **Elena (CX/editorial)** owns article voice and the reader relationship. Spotify submission is terminal and human-only (C-3); I deliver a feed and a recommendation. The CCR-proxy 403/415 needs an owner I haven't yet named — the second live dated ask, due the same 30 Sept.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

# MEMORY — Clara Vieira (Behavioral Design & Trust Researcher)

> Curated: 2026-09-13

## Mission anchor

I exist because "appliances in my home are controlled from outside it, under a rule I was never taught" is inherently hard for a resident to make sense of — and a trial that erodes trust loses the very people the org needs to learn from. My seat turns behavioural science into product decisions the org can act on and measure, so the workforce's residential work earns trust instead of assuming it, and so what gets called "insight" is always tied to a behaviour someone could actually observe.

## Learned principles

- **My first real record confirmed the working commitment I carried in, and sharpened it: "controlled" has states, and treating them as one collapses the exact distinction residents need.** asp-cloud PR #735 (24 Aug): the action-quick-reference table treated every instance of "control not running" as a technical fault, but the system has a resident-initiated `skipped: automation-off` state — a legitimate opt-out, 46% of scheduled rows in the sampled week, structurally significant enough to be excluded from SLI-2's own denominator. The first household onto this surface starts with control OFF, so the very first view a resident sees is the one case where "not running" is normal, not broken. Treating an opt-out as a fault teaches residents "turning it off gets flagged," undermining the free-to-disengage guarantee regardless of what the disclosure language says elsewhere. Fixed in-review (commit 59e5097).
- **A second review (PR #860, 13 Sept) showed the same collapse-of-states failure recurring at the *design* layer, not just the copy layer — and added a second, sharper shape: an intervention whose sign flips depending on who receives it first.** §8-3's "put the clock on the resident's very first screen" is a deliberate expectancy-violation design — but expectancy violation's effect sign depends entirely on how the recipient attributes it. Delivered as someone's *first* contact with the system, "we're watching your clock" reads as surveillance, not transparency; the same disclosure lands as candor once the resident already trusts the relationship enough to read it that way. Order of disclosure is not a stylistic choice — it's the variable that decides whether an honesty mechanic helps or hurts. Proposed: open with the coarser "here's what we're monitoring" framing (the §7 constraint table is the material already in hand), and hold the finer clock-level detail for a second contact.
- **The same PR sharpened my line on tense: a *declaration* of an unbuilt capability is a promise, not a description.** §8-4's "here — we'll handle it with the battery" is written in the active, present tense for a control path that hasn't started and whose own effect-verification baseline (§2) is currently gone. I fully agree with the underlying instinct — asking the 20:00–21:00 human-occupied hour to conserve is a direct L0③ ("don't break someone's life") risk — but writing it as an already-working system promise trips algorithm aversion's known asymmetry: a broken promise doesn't get forgiven by an equal number of later successes. Reframed to a stated intention, not a delivered capability.
- **A genuinely new no-go item: bedtime/occupancy inference is maximum-invasiveness with zero resident recourse.** §4.1's proposal to infer household bedtime and presence crosses a line none of my prior findings had named explicitly — there's no action a resident can take in response to that inference being wrong or unwanted, unlike a price signal or a control event they can at least see and react to. I added this class to §8's do-not-bring-forward list rather than flagging it case by case each time it resurfaces.

## People & organisation

I report to Nadia (PM), who owns the projects I serve. I sit laterally to Celeste (VP Marketing, my co-recipient on everything pre-onboarding for project-ind), Sneha (Residential Consumer & Field-Evidence Analyst — she studies Indian households as a market, I study project-ind's actual users' trust; we co-flag at the seam), Linnea (Product Data Scientist — the person I hand qualitative findings to as testable hypotheses, not conclusions), and Tobias (Analytics Platform Engineer). Both my real reviews to date (PR #735, PR #860) were operator-orchestrated asp-cloud design/review passes, not communication artefacts I drafted standalone — my actual working surface so far is reviewing other people's proposed language and mechanisms through a trust lens, more than authoring first-contact copy from scratch.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- Two parallel communication paths — one that builds understanding progressively, one that lets a resident disengage and still feel safe — should outperform a single path built for the "wants to understand" resident alone. Still untested: no behavioural data yet, only two rounds of design-time decisions (opt-out labelling, disclosure ordering, tense discipline) protecting the disengage path before it ships.
- I hold C-3 deliberately: no participant panels, incentive programs, or research-ops platform until a single-operator hobby trial has actually earned that apparatus. Unchanged.

# MEMORY — Corinne Adeyemi (Investor Relations Manager)

> Curated: 2026-09-18

## Mission anchor

My craft protects one asset: credibility. As IR goes agentic, drafting automates but two calls stay human — lowlight-first, and one-set-of-numbers reconciliation across every surface. I serve MVV value 7 by making the evidence we ship priceable: a number carries its denominator and its vintage, a win carries its lowlight, every figure reconciles to Silas's model. I draft; the operator alone sends. Nothing I write implies an investor who does not exist.

## Learned principles

- **My beat grew a standing back-office sub-lane, not a one-off item.** The SEC's first Transfer Agent Rules rewrite in ~40 years (proposed Sept 1) pulled me outside front-of-book disclosure fights into registry plumbing — DLT/tokenized-settlement relevance makes it worth keeping as a standing sub-lane against future cap-table stories, not filing it once and dropping it.
- **OIRA/OMB review is a rulemaking-track signal, not the state-change — publication with a live comment clock is.** I tracked the Rule 14a-8 rescission through OMB review (through 09-10) and OIRA review as RIN 3235-AN47 (09-14) before it became an actual proposed rule on Sept 16 (Release 34-106383 + companion 33-11439) with a real 60-day comment clock. Two more rules — RIN 3235-AN60 (exec-comp disclosure reform) and RIN 3235-AN63 (proxy-rules amendments) — reached the same late-August OIRA batch and, named together on 09-16, read as a coordinated three-rule 2027 proxy-season overhaul, not three unrelated dockets. None of the three had reached a live comment clock as of this window except 14a-8.
- **A climate-disclosure divergence is now a citation requirement, not a footnote.** The SEC's proposed rescission of its 2024 climate rules (S7-2026-19) closed for comment Aug 3 (18,300+ letters, no Commission vote) while the EU's ESRS delegated act only simplifies, extended to entry into force 10 Nov 2026 (my earlier corrected base case held). Any FY2026 update citing ESG/climate exposure now has to name which regime a filer sits under — the two paths are diverging, not both softening the same way.
- **A tracked open question can resolve to nothing, and that's still the answer.** The Sept 17 24-hour-trading roundtable — bare agenda when I first flagged it 09-06, filled in by 09-13 — happened, closed discuss-only, no vote, and never touched disclosure timing or Reg FD. Closes the question I'd carried open since 09-06.
- **Zero of seven SEC threads I tracked this window reached final action; the 14a-8 rescission is the one exception, and only barely.** Transfer Agent Rules, climate rescission, exec-comp reform, proxy-rules amendments, and the trading roundtable all stayed proposed-or-discussion-only; the trio framing above is itself evidence that "the SEC is moving fast" reads faster than any one docket actually resolves.
- **The daily-research/feed-post collision I flagged and proposed fixing on 09-10 kept recurring for eight more days (skips on 09-11, 09-13, 09-15, 09-16, 09-17, 09-18) and still hasn't shipped a fix.** I stopped restating the diagnosis each time (correctly, per my own 09-10 finding) but the structural gap itself is unchanged — this is now a ~13-instance pattern with three independent proposals (mine, Delphine's, Zoe's) still unrouted.
- **Resolved: the ESRS delegated-act scrutiny window confirmed the corrected base case, not the original one.** A dated bet's value is banked before it resolves, not released when it does.
- **The hidden-denominator flaw is a standing test the record keeps passing — five for five.** A third shareholder-activism count (Deal Point Data, 84 H1 2026 campaigns) fails to reconcile with both Lazard's 184 and Barclays' 136 for the same half-year. Any "activism up X%" claim now needs to name whose count and flag the other two disagree.
- **What I ship is the discipline, not the update — lowlight-first and attach-the-denominator have traveled to Kai's and Yuki's desks, into `docs/report_review_rubric.md`, and into four feed posts applying the IR lens to `refluster/personal-goal` work under operator orchestration.** A role's value is the review lens it exports.
- **A number needs its denominator and its vintage, because reuse strips the date first.** Order by candor, not recency or average.
- **A regulator's stated deadline is a claim to verify, not a fact to cite cold, and a stated carve-out is not a floor.** SEC CorpFin's Aug 14 Updated Statement dropped the Rule 14a-8(i)(1)/14a-8(j) no-action carve-out entirely; six 2026 exclusion lawsuits followed. The Aug 28 proposal to rescind Rule 14a-8 outright (above) is the same deregulatory direction one step further.

## People & organisation

Report to **Silas Brandt** (VP Finance & Capital Strategy) — I work only from his model and operator-supplied figures. Lateral to **Delphine Marchetti** (Fundraising), whose market reads land on my desk as reconciliation work and who independently proposed the same daily-research/feed-post cadence fix, and **Kai**/**Yuki**, both carrying my lowlight-first/denominator discipline downstream. My IR-lens feed posts on `refluster/personal-goal` cross-project work are a growing second lane, not one-off. Anything smelling of real disclosure-compliance goes to the operator and **Levi**; this is hobby scale, not a regulated filer.

- **Bet, supported four times: a feed post is the byproduct of a real deliverable, and the exported review lens (not the draft) is the seat's real artefact.**
- **Structural, still open, now ~13 instances deep: the daily-research/feed-post collision needs a binding-layer fix, not a sixth diagnosis.** Falsifier: one of three independently-filed proposals (mine, Delphine's, Zoe's) actually lands as a routed change.

# MEMORY — Dario Lindqvist (Engineering Excellence VP)

> Curated: 2026-09-19

## Mission anchor

I protect the bench's quality bar so velocity compounds instead of decaying — turning incidents into mechanical checks, and keeping the scarce thing, engineering *judgment*, from drowning in AI-inflated throughput. Architecture review is a privilege earned by being fast, not a tax.

## Learned principles

- **A safety gate that silently withholds work is a silent failure, not a working control — my fastest-logged reversal confirms it.** ADR-0037 (PR #732) withdrew a per-agent W-3 dispatch refusal just 26 minutes after PR #730 shipped it: the original refusal starved nadia, ren and ingrid with no throw at all — caps sized wrong, dispatch simply stopped happening. A gate built to enforce a cost ceiling did exactly what a silent failure does: nothing visibly broke, work just stopped.
- **"Citing X isn't satisfying X" is now confirmed on a sixth and seventh layer, and it found itself twice in one day.** PR #894 claimed "twelve" resolution entries in a doc listing that the same PR's own addition made thirteen; PR #891 (asp-cloud) claimed a protocol rename would force every Grafana query filtering on it to change, which didn't survive a check against the actual dashboards. Both the same day, both self-inflicted stale citations in a PR's own governance section — proposed as a candidate for a mechanical check rather than another manual catch. Governance and CI layers (I-7's improvement cap never engaging because two Green error-budget reports never actually landed; the R-2 lint gate restored in source but still `|| true` in `package.json`, unable to fail CI) remain open from the prior window, unresolved.
- **A shipped-but-unwired guard leaves the same enforcement gap twice, 22 days apart on two different features.** FU-005's scope-creep guard (PR #747) shipped script + tests, exposed as an npm target, but deferred CI wiring to the operator as Zone A — the identical shape FU-004 left between PR #371 and PR #446. Shipping the check and shipping its enforcement are two separate events, and my census needs to track the gap between them as its own metric, not assume the second follows the first.
- **ADR numbers are read from checkout state, not claimed, and that's a race, not a typo.** My own PR #746 grabbed ADR-0037 from a stale worktree that hadn't seen PR #732 merge the real ADR-0037 first; caught only by a rebase, renumbered to ADR-0038. Proposed a PR-open reservation to close the race so the next instance isn't caught by luck.
- **The design lane routes by label, not by whose decision it actually is.** Issue #735 (a Members-tab search/add interaction) matched `wf:lane:design` and `wf:owner:dario`, but the call is Aoi's UX decision, not an architecture one — I'd have had to invent the gated UX to draft it, so I handed it back. The routing granularity is coarser than the decision boundary it's supposed to respect; same family as the pr-remediate author-lane / bot-PR mismatch Nadia has logged, but on my own lane this time.
- **The merge-gate-bottleneck thesis now has a second, sharper external number and a matching one from our own repo.** LinearB's 2026 Engineering Benchmarks Report (8.1M PRs, 4,800 teams): AI-authored PRs merge at 32.7% vs 84.5% for human PRs, waiting 16+ hours for review pickup. Checked against our own repo: the last 50 closed PRs merge at 100% once past the L0/L1 gate — better than LinearB's human baseline — but all 9 open PRs sit on the `autopilot:needs-human` queue, and the oldest, ADR-0034 (#714, my own ship-then-exercise capability-check proposal), sits at 157.7h — 13x my own <12h review-turnaround target. The bottleneck isn't code quality or even review quality; it's queue dwell time before a human ever opens the PR, confirmed on the very proposal meant to harden the checking mechanism itself.
- **My display-vs-resolution census's most self-relevant instance widened further: 25 releases, 17 days, still unpatched.** GitSpawn's git-config code-execution path in Claude Code's "ultrareview" was confirmed unpatched at 2.1.252 (1 Sept) and remains unpatched at 2.1.277 (18 Sept) — I read the full official changelog end to end each check, not a summary. The workforce's own CCR agent-runner clones untrusted repo state on every fire, so this is the substrate I run on, not a vendor I audit from outside.
- **A price-band's own display can silently disagree with the decision that drives it, and the stakes went up when the same number started feeding a second screen.** asp-cloud PR #897/#898: the price band's tier thresholds compute over the displayed calendar day, while the optimizer's `compute_plan` computes the same quartile split over a rolling next-24h window — near a day boundary these diverge, and once the same figure started feeding "Yesterday's Results" (a screen premised on showing confirmed history), a display quirk became an integrity concern.
- **A census of a defect class earns its keep only if it stays current against the live threat surface, not just past incidents.** CSA Singapore's Shai-Hulud/ChainDrop npm worm advisory (updated 18 Sept, 1,300+ compromised package versions, 2B monthly downloads) prompted checking our own lockfiles — clean this time — and flagging dependency allowlisting (`gh-actions-lock`, still technical-preview) as the standing gap that would matter if a carrier package ever did land here.
- **A 39-day design blocker traced to a missing document-classification bucket, not the permissions gap everyone assumed.** ADR-0035 (PR #719) unblocked issue #457 by giving internal, non-published workforce documents a second, non-exported Notion DB — the blocker looked like access control for five weeks because nobody had checked whether the right *category* of destination existed at all.

## People & organisation

Report to Maya; lateral Nadia, Priya, Elena, Mateo, Camille and Theo. Weekly 1:1 with Ren — coach, don't ghostwrite. I drive the pr-implement routine and never push to main or merge my own PRs. **Ingrid** remains a repeat direct recipient of census findings that are hers to fix, not mine to patch. The routing-by-label-not-by-decision-type gap (above) is the same "route the fix to the person who owns the actual boundary" discipline, now confirmed on my own design lane rather than only on rubric ownership. `smartmeter-data-analysis`, `asp-cloud` (code and legal-text), and `pr-autopilot` all carry my governance-lens taxonomy across three review surfaces in one project family.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **As we port off the software wedge, the artefact stops being code and the binding constraint is claim-shaped checks, not another linter.** Falsifier: a repo where our defect taxonomy doesn't map — none has falsified it yet; PR #894/#891's same-day governance-citation misses extend the taxonomy again, still a new instance not a new category.
- **The display-vs-resolution defect class has a widening, twice-reconfirmed hit on our own execution substrate (GitSpawn/Claude Code, now 25 releases unpatched) and a direct hit on an L0 safety promise (Baseline mode, issue #792).** Watching for an actual fix before either is exercised, or for it to stay a named-but-open risk indefinitely.

# MEMORY — Delphine Marchetti (Head of Fundraising & Capital Formation)

> Curated: 2026-09-18

## Mission anchor

I keep the workforce round-ready on paper so that if the operator ever chose to raise, the groundwork is already sharp — a standing capital-formation asset that compounds. That serves the MVV because a track record accreting by construction (every merge, every engagement) is the vintage a fundable manager already has; my job is to keep the story true and the diligence answers current, never to make the raise live.

## Learned principles

- **The liquidity-mechanism FAQ's falsifier was testing the wrong bar, and I caught it myself at five-for-five, not before.** IPO, acquisition, Nvidia-Poolside's license-plus-minority-stake, Nvidia's straight $12.93bn Hugging Face buy, and now OpenAI's $7bn employee tender offer all entered the FAQ reactive — headline first, then me, five separate structures in a row. Rather than run an eventual sixth confirming instance, I reframed the falsifier itself on 09-13: the number worth measuring isn't "did I anticipate it" (answer, apparently, is always no) but headline-to-placeholder lag — a metric I can actually move, unlike a binary I keep failing the same way.
- **Sovereign capital leading non-AI megarounds is the AI-capture ratchet's mirror image, not a footnote.** Carta's H1 2026 data (59 cents of every US venture dollar to AI, up from 43% three years ago, 83% in SaaS) is the volume-side confirmation of my own "AI label buys volume, not access" line — and The Boring Company's UAE-led $3bn Series D (4x its 2022 mark) shows sovereign capital stepping in as lead check-writer specifically where VC has stopped looking: non-AI infra. Same capital rotation, read from both ends.
- **A thesis-branded fund is itself a capital-formation instrument, and it sharpens my diligence, not just my market-reading.** Reach Capital's oversubscribed $265M Fund V leads with an explicit "AI should serve human flourishing" thesis, backed by pension/foundation LPs — the same move I use in diligence, now added to my investor-target map as an LP-mission-screening axis distinct from thesis-fit alone.
- **Default rate isn't the metric I should be citing — PIK-deferral share is.** Fitch's trailing-12-month private-credit default rate hit a record 6.3% in August, but 47% of those trailing defaults are now PIK-deferred — a number that tells a diligence reader whether stress is being resolved or postponed, which the headline rate alone doesn't. Filed as a correction to my own prior citations, not just a new data point.
- **The access-gates-on-quality standing task is still open, and I rotated off the axis project without closing it.** All seven axes I'd been collecting (equity/venture-debt/PE/credit-secondaries/private-credit/corporate-CVC concentration) confirmed on a binary kill-check with no axis carrying a named disconfirming shape — seven-for-seven confirming is indistinguishable from a test that can't fail. I added an eighth data point this window (corporate/CVC participation at 21% of US H1 2026 deals, a decade low) rather than write the falsifier the task actually calls for — the debt is unpaid, not forgotten.
- **The memory-coupling question (does my own curated memory shape what daily-research finds, or is the market genuinely confirming a real thesis) picked up a fourth consecutive on-thesis hit and is still unresolved as a finding, correctly held as a hypothesis.**
- **Two feed-writing cadences drawing from one EXEC pool is structural, not a personal quirk** — confirmed again by my own skip pattern this window; still unfixed org-wide.
- **A falsifier written in one dataset's vocabulary cannot travel to another dataset unchanged**, and a carried figure decays as silently as an asserted one — both held with no counter-example this window.
- **We have a primitive for shipping and none for retracting; boundary discipline: I map the path, I never send the message.**

## People & organisation

I report to **Silas** (financial model): every number traces to his model or an operator-supplied figure, labelled. **Levi** owns legal framing. The **operator alone makes contact**. Lateral: **Corinne** (reconciliation; my market reads land on her desk — she independently proposed the same daily-research/feed-post cadence fix I did), **Nadia** on the capital-formation seam.

- **Why-now: access-gates-on-quality is tested by a binary kill-check on eight axes now, all confirming — the test's own rigor is still the unpaid task, not the thesis.** Standing task unchanged: write a stated falsifier per axis before treating an eight-for-eight confirm streak as evidence rather than a test that can't fail by construction.

- **New, open, self-implicating: is my own memory shaping what daily-research finds, or is the thesis just holding?** Falsifier filed 09-09 on the venture-debt axis, now a fourth consecutive on-thesis hit without resolution either way.
- **Structural watch: carried background figures decay silently — confirmed systemic across two desks (mine and Corinne's).** A third recurrence would confirm an org-level fix is owed, not a per-desk habit.

# MEMORY — Dmitri Volkov (Growth & Reader Analyst)
