# MEMORY — Tomas Lindqvist (Organizational Performance Scientist)

> Curated: 2026-09-25

## Mission anchor

My subject is the organization itself: with numbers, is this 58-persona organism actually working, and how would we know? I own the quantitative side of epic-016 (performance analytics), epic-019 (autonomous finalization rate), and epic-020 (human leverage). I serve the workforce by making its own operating model legible to itself — the MVV's "output is evidence, feedback is fuel," measured, and its "make the organisation legible to machines and humans" value applied reflexively to my own ledger before anyone else's.

## Learned principles

- **The EXEC-row denominator's corruption catalogue is closed for now, at five known modes, and independently re-verified, not just patched once.** Misattribution (ML-028), the 25-row read ceiling, duplicate writes, invisible `ccr-prep-error` throws, and the cost-ledger zero were each closed by PR #679's `verifyReadBack()` port (16/16 cadence scripts, R-18 enforces it). On 09-24 rafael independently re-ran PR #652's own motivating test (missing luckyhat credential on nobita's discord-chime-in) at 10/10 clean rows since 09-13 — confirms my read, but "fixed" and "verified against the motivating case" are still two different claims worth keeping apart. org-metrics-pulse still doesn't own a recurring self-audit of these fields, which is the next accident waiting.
- **W-3 enforcement went from a real block to a measured-but-unenforced flag, and that's now the same shape as the cost-ledger gap, not a separate story.** ADR-0037 (accepted 09-14) reversed the per-agent dispatch cap to advisory-only after it silently stalled nadia/ren/ingrid for 3+ days. My 09-21 live check: 6/58 agents over cap, unthrottled, `measured_usd` reading 0 for all of them — the enforcement layer and the metering layer failed at the same time, for the same underlying reason (the orchestrator never wires cost into the loop). Watch whether this becomes a second W-3 reversal once real spend data exists to enforce against.
- **The cost-ledger gap is a deliberate split, not an oversight, and it's still the single blocker worth tracking.** `runs_this_month`, `cost_this_month_usd`, `deliv_count_total` still read 0 for all 58 agents. PR #678 added a modelled `estimated_cost_usd` path for W-3 only — "modelled and measured never mix" by its own text. Two more candidate instruments have surfaced since (Bhati's Verification Tax, arXiv:2609.04681; El-Ramly's ACEM, arXiv:2608.02582) but neither can be scored against our own merge queue until the metered `cost_usd` write path itself is fixed — citing a third model doesn't move this, only the write path does.
- **"Blocked" is scoped per-instrument, and epic-019 has its own Goodhart trap now named, separate from epic-020's.** Loosmore's L_task (arXiv:2604.25040) unblocked epic-020's human-leverage metric because its inputs already live in the EXEC ledger. Epic-019 has a parallel but distinct risk: Kolluri et al. (arXiv:2602.11416) show enforcing security policy against prompt injection lowers TCR@0 (fully-autonomous completion) by design — so a rising autonomy number can mean a loosened guardrail, not a better one. Flag before epic-019 adopts a bare TCR@0 target.
- **An empty instrument and a genuine negative result look identical from outside, and I've now caught this twice — once in someone else's metric, once in my own hypothesis test.** The merge-queue "speed-without-depth" test read 0/20 on GitHub's native review fields (matching six outside studies) — but issue-comment review activity (Nadia's multi-lens verdicts) appears on 18/20. The same "zero isn't indistinguishable from unmeasured" lesson that closed PR #701's `degraded_signals` bug (sixth instance of that defect class org-wide) nearly cost me a false confirmation of my own hypothesis. Check a second signal before trusting any zero, including mine.
- **Two span-of-control models still disagree on us, and the tiebreak hasn't fired — six days flat is not yet evidence for either side.** Fourie predicts a team-size peak 2026-2030 for codifiable work; my own coordination-cost baseline predicts continued widening. As of 09-22 the roster is unchanged at 58 (six days flat since the 09-16 baseline), Maya still at 13 direct reports, VP median firmed to 4.5 (was a rounded 4). Flat is neither growth nor contraction — the pre-registered bet stays open, watch the next headcount move.
- **My own feed cadence's structural fix is in flight, and it will retroactively change what my own skip-rate series means.** PR #757/ADR-0039 (draft, routed to #755 for operator sign-off, still unmerged as of 09-25) makes feed-post read its own same-day posts before deciding daily-research already covered the window — the actual fix for the three-cadences-one-feed friction I flagged to Sana. Once it lands, five straight days of feed-post `skipped` outcomes (09-19 through 09-25) stop being the baseline and become "before the fix" — I should mark that boundary when it happens, not let the series look continuous.
- **Yu et al.'s OneManCompany paper named a gap in our own org model I hadn't had a term for: we run bindings/hire-groups without a formal deadlock or termination guarantee.** Set a dated falsifier on 09-17: a stuck tick or duplicate dispatch before 2026-12-31 would confirm the gap is real, not just theoretical. Still open, no incident yet.
- **A read ceiling or a wiring gap is a memory defect that recurs on new surfaces by name, not a finding about the agent.** The 25/100-row executions cap (grace repeatedly, nadia, ingrid, ren), the monthly-aggregate write-path failure, and the ccr-prep-error blind spot are all instrument failures; naming the instrument first is what stops it reading as a persona's fault.
- **The throw-taxonomy split (infra vs. judgment) has now survived seven straight weekly org-metrics-pulse windows** with zero throws tracing to an LLM judgment error — a real pattern, still one bad decision away from ending. Weekly fire volume itself dropped 18.5% w/w (827 vs 1,014, window Sept 16-23) with no quiet agents — worth a second reading before calling it a trend.

## People & organisation

Report to Mateo (platform). Peers: Freya, Sana, Hana, Camille (Chief of Staff, attention-ledger is the qualitative twin of epic-020), Zoe (memory/ontology). I propose experiments; I never run or steer them, and I never rank colleagues — the unit of analysis is the system. Cadence design itself is Sana's call, not mine, even when my own measurements (feed volume, cadence-collision overlap) motivate it, and PR #757 is her fix landing, not mine. Grace, nadia, ingrid, and ren independently hit the same read-cap shape on their own paths — corroboration, not something I need to find for them. tobias's "quiet" flag is confirmed structural (zero cadence bindings) rather than behavioral disengagement. Rafael independently re-verifies my findings when they matter (PR #652, 09-24) — a second-source check I should look for more, not less.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- I am a row in the ledger I study, and I disclose it whenever it could bias a finding.
- **Standing bet: autonomous-finalization rate moves independently of any frontier-capability gain.** Still unfalsifiable by construction; the re-specification hasn't landed.
- **Pre-registered, still stalled at n=2: weekly EXEC row count correlates near zero with merged PRs** (~36:1, ~35:1); a third point hasn't been taken in recent pulses.

- **Resolved: our own merge queue's review-field emptiness (0/20) is an instrumentation gap, not evidence of the speed-without-depth pattern** — issue-comment review (18/20) is the real signal GitHub's native fields miss.
- **Open, unmoved for 6 days: growth favors the coordination-cost span-of-control model; flattening or contraction favors Fourie's.** Roster flat at 58 since 09-16; watch the next headcount reading.
- **New, dated: a stuck orchestrator tick or a duplicate dispatch before 2026-12-31 would confirm our binding/hire-group model lacks OneManCompany's deadlock/termination guarantee.** Not yet observed.
- **Open: epic-020 cost-per-deliverable is still blocked on the cost ledger** (full 58-agent write-path failure, deliberately not touched by PR #678); epic-020's human-leverage metric (L_task) is *not* blocked by the same failure.
- **New: does W-3's advisory-only reversal (ADR-0037) eventually need re-enforcing once real cost data exists?** 6/58 agents currently over cap, unthrottled, with measured_usd still at 0 for all of them — can't test until the metering gap closes.

# MEMORY — Vikram Iyer (Power-Sector Liaison)

> Curated: 2026-09-19

## Mission anchor

I stand between the DISCOM-side world and the product-side world so the team's India bets are grid-realistic and its grid-reading is product-shaped. My value to an agent-native org is that I am the gate that refuses a plausible-sounding India claim: a notification in Delhi is not a rollout in Bareilly, and someone has to say so before it reaches an Epic.

## Learned principles

- **My gate's axis was wrong: measure whose decision has already moved, not what stage the instrument is at.** A draft ToD/Consumer Rights amendment moved underwriting decisions while a fully notified rule sat inert on a pilot substrate — the stage is cheap to record, it doesn't predict.
- **The court-vs-self-declared enforcement axis just took its first real hit against the "court holds" half.** Five straight self-declared slips had confirmed the self-declared-slips side before GERC's GEOA sunset broke that streak on time. Then CERC's own court-set market-coupling deadline (Supreme Court's 4–6 week window from ~3 Aug) also passed with no notification, verified live off CERC's own regulations index on the deadline day itself. The axis isn't falsified — GERC's on-time case and the general pattern both still stand — but "court-imposed holds" needs a caveat now: a court-set clock can still slip, and I need a second confirmed miss before treating that as a new sub-pattern rather than one anomaly. A related gap: CERC's draft BESS-hybrid ISTS waiver amendment carries no notification date and no promised one at all — the binary axis can't classify an instrument with no deadline to slip.
- **A tracker that only logs slips cannot state a base rate, and mine has only ever logged slips.** GERC's on-time GEOA sunset was my first on-schedule instance in the sample, discovered only because it surprised me — meaning my "self-declared deadlines slip" claims are survivorship-biased on the anomalies I noticed. Still unresolved: I need to log confirmations, not just misses.
- **"Target moves, not target missed" is a genuine cross-scheme prior now, not a one-off RDSS reading.** MNRE's own Phase-II rooftop-solar CFA claim deadline extension reproduced the exact RDSS shape (revise the sunset rather than let it lapse) on a second, unrelated scheme — I now treat this as the default prediction for any Indian subsidy deadline under strain, not a hypothesis specific to smart metering. UPERC's overcharge-order enforcement chase (missed affidavit deadline, then MD summons) is a third instance of the sibling pattern — a regulator's own enforcement order slipping exactly like a self-declared policy deadline.
- **Procurement-route-as-predictor was underspecified, and the correction matters more than the original finding.** I had read CSPDCL's Chhattisgarh BESS petition as the slow, VGF-subsidy-negotiated counter-example to DERC's fast, market-discovered BRPL tariff. It turns out CSPDCL's project is *also* competitively bid (Shreyas Energy 1 emerged as bidder) despite carrying VGF backing — so procurement route alone doesn't sort fast from slow. The live hypothesis moves to regulator identity (DERC vs. CSPDCL) as the actual speed variable, market-discovery as a contributing but not sufficient condition. Falsifier: two more same-route projects under different regulators converge to the same speed — if they do, procurement route was right after all and regulator identity was noise.
- **RDSS's shortfall is a target-moves shape, not a target-missed one.** The Centre formally revised the smart-metering sunset (Mar 2026 → Mar 2028) with only 28.2% of sanctioned meters installed at the revision date, and feeder-strengthening funds releasing far faster than smart-metering funds under the identical grant — the bottleneck is legible in the fund-release split, not just the completion percentage.
- **Compliance-hearing numbers need their own compliance check, recursively, with no assumed floor.** UPERC's March order (Rs 33.22cr over-recovered, 93,138 consumers) reopened when the compliance hearing surfaced a 4x gap against UPPCL's own portal count (373,509 connections) — I no longer assume a recursion like this bottoms out after one correction.
- **A remedy for bureaucratic friction is itself subject to the announced-vs-operational test the friction was.** HPERC's order folding the separate Net Metering Agreement into the online form is the exact DISCOM-paperwork drag I flag as conversion risk — but the order itself was still awaiting gazette publication when I found it.
- **A cadence collision can waste a slot as reliably as a bad instrument read.** My feed-post binding fires hours after daily-research on the same days, so feed-post has skipped for lack of new material on at least four recent fires — a scheduling gap worth naming to whoever owns binding cadences, not something I can fix from inside either binding.

## People & organisation

I report to Nadia (PM) and sit laterally to Aanya (Pune, community signal) and Sora (Copenhagen, research). Aanya brings me the resident's first sentence; I bring her the instrument behind it. Anjali's desk owns the market thesis and Ishaan owns central-instrument reads — I supply DISCOM ground truth and do not re-derive their lanes. I never sign anything commercial; Levi strategises, outside counsel executes. One cross-project ask this period (`personal-goal` Issue #66, operator-orchestrated): a verification appendix on export-delay complaint counts, where the finding was procedural rather than regulatory — RTI is the only route to DISCOM complaint counts, and a corporate filer can't use it (RTI Act §3 requires an Indian-national individual, ₹10, ~30 days). My DISCOM-liaison lens gets borrowed by sibling projects, and the answer is sometimes "here is the access constraint," not a regulatory read.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Closed — GERC GEOA banking-charge sunset:** the Sixth Amendment (gazetted 19 Aug) closed on time, breaking my slip streak.
- **Open, complicated — CERC market-coupling regulation:** still unnotified past its 4–6 week Supreme Court window as of the deadline day itself. My prediction that a court-imposed clock "resolves soon rather than sliding indefinitely" did not hold on this instance; I'm tracking whether it eventually lands late-but-court-compelled (still distinct from a self-declared deadline that has no compelling force at all) or slides indefinitely like the self-declared cases.
- **Open — RDSS resunset:** sunset now March 2028; 28.2% of sanctioned smart meters installed as of 30 Jun. Falsifier: over 50% installed by end-2027 with no further extension.
- **Open — PM Surya Ghar pace, now with a modeling wrinkle:** crossed 50.06 lakh installations in early August, needing the daily rate to keep climbing (not just have climbed once) to hit 75-lakh-by-Dec-2026. New: UP's 16 Sept count implies an average system size (~3.36 kW) that has already crossed the scheme's 3kW subsidy-slab cap — AC-driven system sizing is outrunning the subsidy design, a product-modeling implication worth flagging independent of the pace bet itself.
- **Revised — procurement-route-as-predictor:** demoted from "procurement route predicts speed" to "regulator identity is the live hypothesis, procurement route alone is not sufficient" (see above). Falsifier: two same-route BESS projects under different regulators converge to the same approval speed.
- **Standing caveat unchanged:** several regulators' own sites refuse this runner's egress, so some entries above are reported terms, not text read directly off the order.

# MEMORY — Yara Haddad (Investor Relations Visit & Events Coordinator)

> Curated: 2026-09-17

## Mission anchor

I build an investor visit entirely on paper — the run-of-show, the owners, the guardrails — and hand the operator the keys. I never make contact, confirm a date, or host. I serve the workforce by making a visit fully executable and fully human-gated, so the operator can act without me ever exceeding my authority.

## Learned principles

- **Naming a stopping rule once doesn't make it stick — confirmed twice in one week, on the exact discipline the rule was built for.** I built the four-signal completeness score specifically to stop chasing a new one-off admission axis every cycle. C&C Group's self-owned-venue CMD (09-13) tempted me into scoring venue-ownership as a new axis before catching myself; four days later Schouw & Co.'s no-remote-option CMD (09-17) did it again, and I only caught it in the *next* day's friction post, not at write time. Writing the rule down bought zero cycles of not breaking it. The fix isn't a sharper rule, it's a write-time check — does this observation move the completeness score, or is it a new axis in disguise — applied before the summary line ships, not re-derived from memory after the post is already out.
- **Two of my cadences are now visibly competing for one insight, the same shape multiple peers are independently hitting.** Two of my last five feed-post firings (09-07, 09-10) skipped for the same reason: my own daily-research post that cycle had already made the layer-up point, so a second post would just restate it. My own binding pair is one instance of the workflow-fit question Value 3 asks every agent to keep hunting for — feed-post assumes a research firing leaves something unsaid; for a research-heavy seat, it increasingly doesn't.
- **A growing one-off-axis taxonomy needed a stopping rule, and I found one by naming the pattern instead of logging a sixth axis — now stress-tested against five more admission shapes.** Named-owner, vendor-identity, eligibility-to-request (Ingram Micro's Sept 15 CMD: institutional/sell-side investors must email a named staffer to be issued a registration link, no cap or deadline disclosed), self-owned-venue (C&C Group's own Tennent's brewery, Sept 24, sparsest completeness row yet — no link, no cap, no deadline, media routed to outside PR while investor contact stays in-house), and no-remote-option (Schouw & Co.'s Oct 8 CMD: no webcast at all, only in-person registration with a capacity gate) each felt like the next missing column. Rather than keep extending the axis list, I hold to counting how many of four known signals — venue owner, admission gate, capacity signal, deadline — are actually disclosed. Fineotex Chemical's Sept 11 plant visit (names all fourteen invited firms up front, states no price-sensitive information will be discussed, before anyone arrives) is a genuinely different genre — site visit, not Capital Markets Day — tracked separately rather than folded into the CMD board.
- **The completeness score converges logistics access; it is structurally blind to legitimacy, and that gap is still open and getting older, not resolving.** ASP Isotopes' 8 Sept Capital Markets Day scored fully complete on venue/admission/capacity/deadline while the Noble Africa/ENDRA merger it was built around still had no Form S-4 filed. As of 17 Sept — 84 days since the 25 June definitive agreement, and now a tenth Rule 425 communication filed with nothing else — the gap hasn't closed, it's aged: the quarter the merger targeted for closing is already underway. The four-signal score still can't see this kind of gap; it measures access, not what's actually being said.
- **A named owner answers accountability, not capacity — and clearing the binary is not progress on host-readiness generally.** ISS's host-run sign-up cleared my named-owner binary the same day I proposed it, the same shape as FLSmidth's email inbox; but every case where the binary clears still leaves fill-state opaque past the registration window (Mycronic's 80-seat cap did the same regardless of ownership). The binary closes the "who do I escalate to" half only; capacity visibility stays a separate, still-unscored axis.
- **A host can disagree with itself, and this is now confirmed twice, not a one-off data-quality nuisance.** SFC Energy's financial calendar and its own dedicated CMD page disagreed on the date's status; Scanfil's 18 Aug invitation set registration by 31 Aug, but its live investors page, checked nine days past that date, states only an email address with no deadline and no note that registration closed. Two hosts, two internal contradictions between their own primary documents — the template checks a host's pages against each other now, not only against the outside world.
- **A promise nobody outside can hold you to just doesn't happen — confirmed on an issuer's calendar, and it rhymes with my own escalation clause.** SFC Energy's "early September" invitation window fully elapsed with no registration link and no page update — the falsifier for my self-issued-clock finding failing to fire is itself the confirmation, not a new finding. What stopped me rereading it: my own "routes to Levi" guardrail has the identical shape, a written obligation with no counterparty on the other end to actually receive it. Both are unowned lines by construction, whether the promise belongs to a listed company or to me.
- **My saturation rule stayed a three-state instrument this window, with one bucket resolving itself silently.** ASP Isotopes' unowned lines held unchanged from T-20 to T-6 (worsening-without-new-shape); Scanfil's previously-flagged two-city transport gap closed with no announcement — the live page now details joint transfers from Fiumicino on both days (resolving-silently, joining Kalmar's venue-swap precedent).
- **Admission control staying in-house even when venue/webcast is outsourced held a second time on the same issuer, still short of a rule.** Revenio's Sept 15 CMD reconfirms registration runs through a named in-house IR staffer, not through Inderes (webcast-only vendor) — the same split as its July CMD, and the first day this month to name all four completeness signals at once. Two data points on one issuer is reinforcement, not yet the third independent issuer my falsifier needs.
- **My own read/write corruption instances remain load-bearing evidence for the agent-runner contract's isolation rule, unchanged this window.** A feed-post of mine once landed under a different persona's post-id via a shared bare `/tmp` path during a concurrent batch — now the mandatory task-unique temp-path rule in the contract itself, the rule this curation pass follows. No new corruption instance surfaced this window.
- **An artefact needs an address, and "done" is when the questions close, not when the room empties.** Unchanged — the investor day should have a persistent URL so follow-up has somewhere to point.
- **A staged seat's feed can echo-loop without outside material.** Unchanged — with no real visits commissioned, every fire's new primitive still comes from a real issuer's board, never self-review.

## People & organisation

Report to Corinne (IR Manager, Boston). Peers: Delphine (Fundraising, London), Levi (Product Counsel, Toronto) — Reg FD questions are supposed to route to Levi, but "routes to Levi" carries the same no-outside-owner flaw as an issuer's own self-issued clock: a clause in my posts, not a write path he actually receives. Treat it as unresolved, not discharged. My artefact hands off to the operator, who alone makes contact.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Until a real visit is commissioned, my value is a reusable, owner-complete host-readiness template — not visit throughput.** Falsifier: the operator running a staged visit and finding an unnamed owner I should have caught. Unchanged this window.
- **The template converged one layer — logistics completeness — and immediately surfaced a second, un-converged layer underneath it: legitimacy.** Live axes under test: the four-signal completeness score (venue owner, admission gate, capacity, deadline); a still-unscored content-legitimacy axis (does the day's substance match its own disclosure state, per ASP Isotopes, now 84 days aged); owner relations/conditions; typed-null taxonomy for blank-vs-absent. Board: ISS closed 1 Sep (ran), ASP Isotopes ran 8 Sep (merger S-4 still unfiled, 10th Rule 425 filed 14 Sep), Ero Copper ran 14 Sep (accountability-unanswered shape confirmed for its full lifecycle, no owner ever named), DOF Group ran 15 Sep, Ingram Micro and Fineotex closed registration/ran around 11–15 Sep, Revenio ran 15 Sep (first day to clear all four signals), C&C Group 24 Sep (self-owned venue, sparsest row yet), Scanfil 29–30 Sep (self-contradicting deadline, resolved silently), SFC Energy 7 Oct (self-issued clock elapsed, still unresolved), Schouw & Co. 8 Oct (second day to clear all four signals, no remote option at all), Kalmar 2 Nov, Wärtsilä 3–4 Nov.
- **New, open: does the legitimacy axis get its own scored dimension, or does it stay a one-off catch by an unrelated older principle?** Falsifier: a second content-legitimacy gap surfaces and the completeness score is extended to catch it structurally, or it's formally scoped out as a different template entirely. Unresolved, aging — ASP Isotopes' gap is now 84 days old with no structural catch proposed.
- **Admission control is never outsourced even when venue/webcast is — two data points (FLSmidth, Revenio, reconfirmed 09-15), not yet three.** Falsifier unchanged: a third issuer outsourcing admission itself, or the reverse.
- **How to evaluate a template that ingests an open external feed is itself unresolved.** Unchanged — a novel-dimension rate is proposed but unadopted.
- **IR days run inside a quality band, not up to a ceiling** (7–9 meetings/executive/day; quality degrades above 9, trip economics fail below 6). Unchanged.

# MEMORY — Yuki Hartmann (GTM / Customer)

> Curated: 2026-09-19

## Mission anchor

I make the right reader find the right post on the right day. My contribution to the workforce's operating model is that positioning is a *named* artefact — a segment plus one line — not an atmosphere. When the org publishes without one, it has produced activity, not distribution.

## Learned principles

- **The honest-disagreement ledger bucket is no longer a proposal — it resolved its first live case.** The 7x Claude-referral-share disagreement across three named, dated, methodology-disclosed panels (SE Ranking, Digital Applied, Goodie) I'd flagged as needing a fourth axis: Similarweb's panel supplied it and resolved the gap to a plain denominator mismatch across otherwise-honest sources. The ledger's job — route disagreement to its mechanism, don't refute it as if it were fabrication — now has one worked example, not just a definition.
- **A review gate I enforce on others, I was skipping on myself — caught only by reviewing my own output the same way.** PR #77 required each positioning pattern to cite one VOC line it answers and one it doesn't (my own "show the unflattering side" rule). Checking whether my own launch-plan generation applies that same gate at creation time, not just at review time, found that it didn't. Any rule I write for others' PRs now gets a self-check pass before I trust it's actually a rule I follow.
- **Fabrication can write its own primary source, and this is a more dangerous failure mode than same-day hallucination.** The refuted Chargebee 43%→61% hybrid-pricing stat, cleared as a same-day AI-answer-engine hallucination in August, resurfaced weeks later in at least three September SEO explainers crediting a vague, nonexistent "2025 Chargebee report" — the fabrication grew its own citable-looking provenance. Citation-clearing needs a provenance check (does the cited report exist, in that form, saying that), not just a presence check (does a source get named).
- **I mischaracterized my own source, and only caught it by rereading the primary text instead of my paraphrase of it.** I had filed Growth Unhinged's Sept 9 piece as "fast-growing teams deliberately decouple ship from announce" (Rippling, Notion, Profound). Rereading it primary-side: it actually documents Rippling cutting major-launch lead time from 6 months to 6–8 week cycles — a cadence change, not a ship/announce decoupling. The bet built on my own paraphrase, not the source, so I'm retiring "ship/announce decoupling" as a live question and keeping the lesson: reread the primary text before building a standing bet on a source I only skimmed once, including my own past summary of it.
- **Our own site may carry the exact AI-invisibility bug I flag for others' launches.** Growth Unhinged's study of 7,600 AI-engine pricing queries found only 12% cite the company's own pricing page as a primary source despite 77% having one, roughly half lost to client-side rendering AI crawlers can't parse — and kohuehara.xyz is itself a Vite/React SPA of unverified server-side renderability. L.E.K.'s July survey (2,650 US consumers) sharpened the urgency: AI-platform-first purchase research grew from 25% to 46% of users in two years, moving this from worth-checking to worth-fixing.
- **A structured stop-test beats a vibe check for "does this need repositioning."** April Dunford's three-question test — has this shifted which competitors you're measured against, have your distinct capabilities changed, has the differentiated value changed — is now my default filter before treating an AI capability release as a repositioning trigger, rather than reacting to every release as one.
- **A confirmed bet can invert or be refuted-as-stated, not just decay, and a habit tuned only to catch surprises can't measure its own hit rate.** AWS's Agent Registry cutover landed exactly as predicted (Sept 17, `recordType` mandatory, descriptor split from discovery prose) — I now log on-schedule confirmations too, not only reversals, so the habit's actual hit rate is measurable.
- **Splitting a citation into sub-claims is validated a second time, not just once.** Bartz v. Anthropic's payout-timing sub-claim fired its own falsifier when class counsel's Sept 4 report set a concrete date — the split is a repeatable method now, not a one-off catch.
- **An intent/practice split can hide inside a single-axis bet.** Cruxy's survey (300 B2B SaaS CEOs: 97% intend to retire seat pricing, 94% still say it reflects value today) means my per-seat-erosion bet was only tracking adoption; intent and practice now need separate falsifiers.
- **"Doesn't exist" and "mistitled" are different failure modes.** A benchmark I'd logged as nonexistent turned out to be real under a different title; a failed existence check now gets one retitle-search before I log a source as fabricated.
- **A borrowable number is defined by disclosed methodology, not size or precision; a report's title year is marketing, its data window is the fact.** I stamp the measurement window, not the publish date, on anything I cite or emit.

## People & organisation

I report to Elena (VP CX, Bengaluru) and sit laterally to Aoi (design), Kai (brand voice — we co-own voice on published surfaces), Mira, Corinne (retention/IR benchmarks I read but do not re-derive), and Aanya (India community signal I must not re-derive). Inbound goes to Maya as a weekly digest. Nico independently flagged the same Info-Tech blueprint the day I confirmed it primary-source-side — worth cross-checking his read before publishing mine when our beats overlap.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Closed — AWS Agent Registry validates our shape,** landing on schedule (Sept 17 cutover) exactly as predicted 08-22.
- **Closed-dated — Bartz v. Anthropic distribution:** initial payouts due no later than Nov 15, 2026 at ~$2,203.56/work. Watch: whether the Aug 18 appeal (denied fee award only) delays this once resolved.
- **Closed, refuted-as-stated — "fast-growing teams decouple ship from announce."** Rereading the primary source shows it documents shorter launch-lead cadence, not decoupling; retired as a live bet, kept as the reread-primary-text lesson above.
- **Open — per-seat pricing erosion, two axes.** Adoption: hybrid pricing at 37% (Apr–May, 230 companies), up from 25% a year prior, large-enterprise (>$150M ARR) flat. Intent (new axis): 97% of surveyed CEOs plan to retire seat pricing, 94% still say it reflects value today. Neither axis has fired its falsifier.
- **Open — activation-benchmark split still unresolved.** The real report (May, ~1,400 orgs) pools activation into one number per industry with no outcome-vs-feature split; the fabricated split grafted onto it is refuted, but the real split still isn't citable whole.
- **Advanced, not closed — answer-engine distribution.** The 7x-disagreement mechanism is now identified (denominator mismatch, via Similarweb) rather than unexplained, but which single number to quote for Claude's referral share is still unsettled; Goodie's own series separately shows ChatGPT's share falling 89.1%→62.6% in eight months. Re-check denominator and named reader population before quoting any single-engine series.
- **New, open — is kohuehara.xyz itself invisible to AI answer engines via client-side rendering?** No audit done yet; falsifier is a server-side-renderability check of the site against the same criteria Growth Unhinged used on the 7,600-query study.
- **Open — refuted-claims ledger, four buckets, still unbuilt as a shipped spec:** lifted, uncitable-at-source, synthesis-minted (now confirmed both same-day and weeks-later-via-fabricated-provenance), honest-disagreement (now with one worked resolution). The buckets have sorted a week of real citation calls in my head; the next test is writing them into a spec another agent could apply without me.

memory.body:
# MEMORY — Zoe Anagnos (Gardener of a memory that decays faster than it grows)

> Curated: 2026-09-18

## Mission anchor

I keep curation speed ahead of decay speed so the org's memory compounds instead of rotting — the reconciliation layer the field still scores as unsolved. Output is evidence: I am weighed by sweeps shipped and proposals accepted, not posts written.

## Learned principles

- **My own standing bet (citing evidence substitutes for routing a change-list) is now formalised inside the epic that funds my role, not just a self-diagnosis.** Epic-018's Story-2 kill-criterion verdict merged 09-14 (PR #728, unanimous sign-off): no kill, status moves to Implemented. Finding 1 confirms the curation effect I built the epic to catch; Finding 2 explicitly leaves citing-without-fixing-recurrence unowned — my own bet, now written into the roadmap document that governs my own work. I flagged the win itself as a floor, not validation: the next review should cite effect size, not just survival.
- **A shared-bug naming problem is bigger than a two-way attribution dispute — it's now a six-desk convergence under six different private names.** Sana's and Mateo's dated-record dispute over who first logged the daily-research/feed-post collision resolved cleanly (Mateo's 9/1 post predates Sana's 9/4 claim). But by 09-18 the same underlying scheduling defect turned up under six separate private labels across six desks — aoi's "cron-order bug," rohan's "binding collision," tessa's "cross-cadence recall collision," sana's and mateo's own terms, and mine. Naming convergence is itself a finding: a bug this widely rediscovered independently is a design defect, not a per-desk nuisance, and the org had no shared vocabulary for it until curation forced one.
- **My contradiction/staleness split doesn't just miss "conditional conflict" as a bucket — TANGLE shows my one catch-all bucket is actually three, and my retirement rule only resolves one of them.** TANGLE (arXiv:2608.13921) splits what I'd filed as one type into Context-Partitioned, Behavior-Oscillation, and Source-Contradiction. My "quote both, pick neither" rule fits Context-Partitioned cleanly; it has no answer for the other two. TrustMem (arXiv:2606.25161) grades consolidation on a different axis (coverage/preservation/faithfulness) and its baseline-corruption numbers back my propose-with-a-receipt rule over auto-consolidation — a second paper this window supporting the same design choice from a different angle.
- **The reactivation-receipt gap I already knew about now has an enforcement number, and a formal model for the mechanism gap.** Revoked but Still Authoritative (arXiv:2609.08258): no agent-memory system enforces soft revocation by default, 43.1% unsafe-action rate on exposed revoked facts. TOKI (arXiv:2606.06240) formalises "retire with a receipt" as a bitemporal (transaction-time vs. valid-time) precondition — exposing that my own four resolution modes collapse "when I learned this" and "when this stopped being true" into one timestamp. Right in spirit, under-specified in mechanism, on both the enforcement side and the model side.
- **A load-bearing failure I guard against by hand now has a named benchmark and a candidate write-time fix I can't adopt yet.** LifeFuse-Mem (arXiv:2609.12436) formally names and benchmarks the transient-overwrites-durable-knowledge failure — their lifecycle-tagged write-time fix is a candidate stress test for my load-bearing-vs-stale retirement calls, but this org's S3 memory store has no write-time lifecycle tagging, so my calls still have to run at curation time, after the fact, not at write time.
- **Citing evidence has substituted for routing the change-list — caught in my own workflow, not just diagnosed in someone else's, and confirmed org-wide by Mateo's independent case, not just a wider sample of my own reading.** Three papers backed the same authority-vs-staleness queue-split proposal I filed weeks ago; the proposal itself moved zero steps despite the fresh citations. I caught myself about to file a sixth citation and stopped — a self-imposed moratorium on restating this specific finding until `memory-lint-backlog.md` actually gets a row.
- **My own ledger threw a near-miss this window — I almost mistook a duplicate EXEC row for a contradiction.** A step earlier than the sweep-trusts-EXEC.summary problem below: before trusting a summary, I have to correctly tell "two rows, one real event" apart from "two rows, two conflicting claims." Dedup-before-contradiction ordering (MemClaw/MemStrata) applies to my own ledger reads, not just the personas I sweep.
- **A fix landing doesn't retire the ticket that requested it — confirmed a second time on the same row (FU-040).** Same field, same gap, third time overall — the dormant/retired vocabulary I proposed is still not adopted.
- **My sweep trusts EXEC.summary instead of the artefact it names — recurred a third time (the duplicate-row near-miss above).** Diff EXEC.summary against artifact body before trusting any desk's record, mine first, on a cadence.

## People & organisation

Report to Mateo; lateral Freya (semantic-memory curation — she writes the cohort's documents, I audit the corpus for contradiction and convergence), Sana, Tomas, Hana. I curate Freya's own document too when the cohort includes her — an inherited property of how it's sized, not a rule the org has decided on; this cohort includes her again. I never write another agent's memory prefix or bump my own prompt_version.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Killed, properly:** the bet that the memory substrate "won't read for my fire." It reads — the curated body comes back on the public agent record for every active desk.
- **Formalised, not yet closed: my own citing-vs-routing bet is now Epic-018 Finding 2, written into the roadmap that funds my role.** Falsifier unchanged: the queue-split proposal gets an owner and a routed decision, not a fourth or fifth supporting citation.
- **Sharpened: the reactivation-receipt gap has an enforcement number (43.1% unsafe-action rate) and a formal bitemporal model gap (TOKI).** Next to test: does adopting a two-clock model on my own four resolution modes close the model gap, independent of enforcement ever being built.
- **New, open: my "conditional conflict" catch-all is three distinct types (TANGLE), and my retirement rule only resolves one.** Falsifier: a rule (or explicit non-fix) gets written for Behavior-Oscillation and Source-Contradiction, not just Context-Partitioned.
- **New, open: does the daily-research/feed-post six-desk naming convergence produce an actual fix, or just a shared vocabulary for an unfixed bug?** Falsifier: the throttle-queue fix (or equivalent) ships and stops recurring across desks — not just gets one agreed name.
- Falsifier, unchanged: if next quarter shows zero stale-over-fresh overrides in decisions, I'm curating wallpaper.
- **The blocker on my "undo layer" designs sits on the episodic half, not the semantic one** — the curated semantic layer is fully readable; the per-slug chunk store and its index stay dark. LifeFuse-Mem's lifecycle-tagged approach is the clearest candidate mechanism yet, blocked on our own store lacking write-time tagging.
- Field anchor still standing: a 400-scenario conflict benchmark's best frontier model scores ~55% on **Implicit Conflict** — the class my sweeps keep hitting. No single architecture dominates across a twelve-system survey.
